qs.q: An inherited defect in renal tubular amino acid transport causes cystinuria, characterized by recurrent nephrolithiasis. Which shared transport system is dysfunctional in both the proximal renal tubule and the intestinal lumen?
o: A sodium-dependent neutral amino acid symport carrier
A facilitated diffusion carrier selective for acidic residues
An ATP-binding cassette transporter specific for aromatic rings
A chloride-coupled exchanger mediating small peptide uptake
A basic and dibasic amino acid apical membrane transporter
qs.e: Cystinuria involves defective reabsorption of cystine and dibasic amino acids via a shared renal and intestinal transport system.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Clinical Biochemistry Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A 50-year-old man with a history of radiation therapy to the neck twenty-five years ago presents with nephrolithiasis and elevated serum calcium. What is the most frequent pathological finding expected in his parathyroid glands?
qs.e: While neck irradiation is a known risk factor, a single adenoma remains by far the most frequent cause of primary hyperparathyroidism overall at 85 to 90 percent. Four-gland hyperplasia accounts for only 10 to 15 percent of cases.
qs.s: Hyperparathyroidism: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary and Parathyroid: MCQs

qs.q: A 24-hour urine collection is ordered for the quantitative assessment of mineral balance in a patient with recurrent nephrolithiasis. Which chemical preservative must be added to the container prior to collection when testing for urinary calcium and magnesium?
qs.e: Acidifying the urine prevents the precipitation of calcium and magnesium salts against the container walls. Acetic acid is insufficient to maintain the necessary low pH for this specific mineral fraction.
qs.s: Specimen and Sample Handling in Clinical Diagnosis: MCQs

qs.q: A 32-year-old patient presents with recurrent nephrolithiasis, a symptomatic pancreatic islet cell tumor, and a prolactinoma. Genetic screening is likely to reveal a mutation in which gene?
qs.e: The patient exhibits the classic 3 Ps of MEN1 syndrome (Parathyroid, Pancreas, Pituitary), which is caused by a mutation in the MEN1 gene on chromosome 11q13. RET proto-oncogene mutations are instead associated with MEN2 syndromes.
qs.s: Adrenal Neoplasms and MEN Syndromes: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following medications is contraindicated in patients with nephrolithiasis or moderate to severe chronic kidney disease?
qs.e: Probenecid, a uricosuric agent, is explicitly stated to be contraindicated in nephrolithiasis and moderate to severe CKD. Allopurinol and febuxostat are xanthine-oxidase inhibitors and are not contraindicated in these conditions.

qs.q: A patient is evaluated for nephrolithiasis and found to have changes in urinary pH predisposing to stone formation. Which urinary pH shift directly promotes the deposition and precipitation of calcium stones?
qs.e: An alkaline urinary pH promotes calcium deposition and stone formation, whereas an acidic pH favors the precipitation of uric acid stones. Maintaining adequate fluid intake helps keep the urine dilute regardless of pH.
qs.s: Kidney Function Tests & Gastric Function: MCQs

qs.q: A 50-year-old male with a history of recurrent joint pain and gout presents with a kidney stone composed of uric acid. Which therapeutic intervention is specifically utilized to prevent the recurrence of uric acid nephrolithiasis by altering urinary chemistry?
qs.e: Alkalinization of the urine is used specifically to prevent uric acid stones because acidic environments promote uric acid crystallization. Conversely, potassium citrate and thiazides are used to prevent calcium stones.
qs.s: Kidney Function Tests & Gastric Function: MCQs

qs.q: A 24-hour urine collection is ordered for a patient with recurrent nephrolithiasis to evaluate uric acid excretion. Which chemical additive is traditionally added to maintain the solubility of urate?
qs.e: Sodium hydroxide is used to provide alkalinization, which enhances the solubility of uric acid in urine. Hydrochloric acid is instead used to preserve calcium and magnesium.
qs.s: Clinical Biochemistry: Core Concepts and Laboratory Principles: MCQs
